summary: Implemented automatic shared-prefix cascade decode for the eager FlashInfer attention path. Eligible batches are split into one shared-prefix page table and per-request suffix page tables, evaluated with paged prefill kernels, and combined with FlashInfer's numerically stable merge_state operation. The implementation preserves per-layer sm_scale, logits_soft_cap, k_scale, and v_scale. Unsupported configurations fall back to the existing decode path.

See reports/j-7631c937bde1/raw/cascade-unit-gpu-final2.log and reports/j-7631c937bde1/raw/environment-gpu.log. FlashInfer itself was not executed because the pinned ROCm environment has no flashinfer module.
remaining_limitations: The assigned node is AMD MI350X/ROCm 7.2 and the pinned environment has no flashinfer package, so the actual NVIDIA FlashInfer kernels, JIT/native artifacts, and end-to-end FlashInfer serving path could not be executed.

Cascade decode is currently eager-only. CUDA-graph replay continues to use the existing decode wrapper because graph selection is keyed only by batch size while common-prefix eligibility and length vary per replay; a correct graph implementation needs a cascade-aware graph variant/key and capture-stable buffers.
Sliding-window attention, encoder-decoder cross attention, speculative decode, and dequant-workspace KV cache configurations deliberately retain the existing non-cascade path.

No model-weight serving benchmark was run. The qualified tiny Llama fixture validates transport/engine execution but cannot exercise FlashInfer on this ROCm-only node, so using it would not strengthen the kernel claim.
No native library was changed or rebuilt.
